info.title: warden
info.description:
The HTTP contract of warden, the identity and audit library for Cognisn products. A product mounts warden's routers under prefixes it chooses; this document shows them under the defaults (`/auth`, `/admin`, `/audit` and `/keys`). What a client must do with these routes (token storage, refresh, the uniform refusal, single sign-on, the throttle) is in `docs/guide/clients.md`.

Routes under `/audit` and the single sign-on administration routes under `/admin/sso` are guarded by an authorisation dependency the product supplies; their refusals are the product's own.

post.summary: Sign in with an email address and password
post.description: Answers with a new session (`status` `signed_in`), or with a challenge when a second factor is needed: `mfa_required` (send a TOTP code to `/totp/verify`, a security key's answer to `/webauthn/verify`, or a recovery code to `/recovery-code`; `methods` lists the kinds the user holds) or `mfa_enrolment_required` (enrol through `/totp/enrolment` or `/webauthn/registration` under the challenge). An unknown address, a wrong password, an `sso_only` user, a user who is not active and a throttled attempt all get the uniform refusal, in the same time.

401.description: The uniform refusal. Every authentication failure on every identity route answers with these exact bytes, headers and status, with indistinguishable timing; the reason is recorded only in the audit trail.

post.summary: Complete sign-in with a TOTP code
post.description: Sends the `mfa_required` challenge with a six-digit code. A code is accepted at most once per time step; too many wrong codes end the challenge.

401.description: The uniform refusal. Every authentication failure on every identity route answers with these exact bytes, headers and status, with indistinguishable timing; the reason is recorded only in the audit trail.

post.summary: Complete sign-in with a recovery code
post.description: Sends the `mfa_required` challenge with one unused recovery code, which is used up, even under concurrent requests.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new session pair
post.description: Refresh tokens rotate: each is single-use and the answer carries its replacement. Presenting a token that was already used ends its whole family (every token descended from the same sign-in), except that the immediate predecessor presented within the session policy's reuse grace window is refused without ending it. Refused for a user who is no longer active.

post.description: Needs an access token as the bearer token. Ends the user's other sessions; the current one stays. A wrong current password, or a user without a password (`sso_only`), gets the fixed 400 message `password change refused`.

post.summary: Begin signing in with a passkey
post.description: Answers with the options for `navigator.credentials.get()`: a fresh, single-use challenge, user verification required and no `allowCredentials`, so the answer is the same for every caller and reveals nothing about any account. The browser offers the user's passkeys, from a button or through conditional mediation (`mediation: "conditional"` with `autocomplete="username webauthn"`). No request body. Throttled by source address: once the address has made `identity.sign_in_attempt_limit` requests within `identity.sign_in_window_seconds`, the uniform refusal and no challenge. A passkey sign-in from the address clears the count. Without WebAuthn configured, the uniform refusal.

401.description: The uniform refusal. Every authentication failure on every identity route answers with these exact bytes, headers and status, with indistinguishable timing; the reason is recorded only in the audit trail.

post.summary: Sign in with a passkey
post.description: Sends the browser's answer to `navigator.credentials.get()` for options from `/passkey/options`. Answers with a new session (`status` `signed_in`) whose `amr` is `["hwk", "mfa"]`, which satisfies a session policy that requires a second factor: there is no second step. Open to `password_and_sso` and `passkey_only` users, with a passkey: a discoverable credential registered with user verification. Each options' challenge is accepted once. Every failure (an unknown credential, a user handle that does not match, a user who is not active or is `sso_only`, a key that did not verify the user or is not a passkey, a signature counter that did not increase, a bad signature, a used or expired challenge, a throttled attempt) gets the uniform refusal.

post.summary: Accept an invitation with a password
post.description: Sets the password, activates the user and applies the staged roles, using the link up. It does not sign the user in: sign in next. A bad, used or expired token, or a user who is no longer invited (which uses the link up), gets the uniform refusal. A password that is too short is a 400, and an invitation that must be accepted through single sign-on or with a passkey is a 409; both leave the link usable.

post.summary: Accept an invitation by registering a passkey
post.description: Sends the browser's answer to `navigator.credentials.create()` for options from `/invitations/accept/passkey/options`, and an optional nickname. Registers the passkey, activates the user, applies the staged roles and uses the link up, in one transaction. Answers with the passkey and fresh recovery codes, shown once. It does not sign the user in: sign in with the passkey next (`POST /passkey/options`). An answer that is not a passkey is a 400 and leaves the link usable; so is an invitation accepted another way (409). A bad, used or expired token, or a user who is no longer invited (which uses the link up), gets the uniform refusal.

post.description: Always 202, answered before any work is done, identically for every address, so neither the answer nor its timing reveals whether an account exists. A link is mailed only to an active user who signs in with a password; earlier links stop working.

get.description: A top-level browser navigation. Stores a login transaction (PKCE S256, state and nonce), sets the login binding cookie and redirects to the identity provider. Every failure lands the browser on `http.sso_completion_link` with `?error=sso_failed` and nothing else, clearing the cookie; show `SSO_FAILURE_MESSAGE`. The reason is recorded only in the audit trail (`warden.identity.sso.sign_in`).

302.description: To the provider; on failure, to the completion link.

set-cookie.description: `__Secure-warden-sso`, the login binding: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, path `<auth prefix>/sso`, for `sso.login_transaction_ttl_seconds`.

400.description: A failure while `http.sso_completion_link` is not configured: the fixed failure message as plain text.

text/plain.example: Single sign-on did not complete. Try again, or contact your administrator.

post.summary: Accept an invitation through single sign-on
post.description: The product's accept-invitation screen submits the link's token as `invitation`, a urlencoded form (a top-level form submission) or a JSON object, chosen by `Content-Type`, so the token appears in no URL. The token is sealed into the login transaction to this browser's binding. At the callback the verified identity accepts the invitation (it must be the invited address), and the browser lands like any sign-in. Any other content type, or a missing, repeated or malformed `invitation`, is a failure. Every failure lands the browser on `http.sso_completion_link` with `?error=sso_failed` and nothing else, clearing the cookie; show `SSO_FAILURE_MESSAGE`. The reason is recorded only in the audit trail (`warden.identity.sso.sign_in`).

get.description: The redirect URI registered with the provider: `http.public_base_url` + `http.auth_prefix` + `/sso/callback`. Uses the login transaction up, redeems the code with the PKCE verifier, validates the id_token and matches a pre-provisioned active user, then lands the browser on `http.sso_completion_link` with only a one-time handoff code (`?code=`). Every failure lands the browser on `http.sso_completion_link` with `?error=sso_failed` and nothing else, clearing the cookie; show `SSO_FAILURE_MESSAGE`. The reason is recorded only in the audit trail (`warden.identity.sso.sign_in`).

post.summary: Set a user's sign-in method
post.description: `password_and_sso`, `sso_only` or `passkey_only`. An `sso_only` or `passkey_only` user cannot sign in with, reset or change a password; a `passkey_only` user signs in with a passkey alone (`POST /passkey/sign-in` under the auth prefix). Setting `passkey_only` also answers `has_passkey`: when false, the user cannot sign in until they register a passkey from a link (`POST /users/{user_id}/passkey-registration`). `sso_only` is refused (409) while the user holds security keys or passkeys: reset their second factors first (`DELETE /users/{user_id}/mfa`).

delete.summary: Reset every second factor of a user
delete.description: For a user who has lost their second factors. In one transaction it removes the TOTP enrolment (confirmed or not), every security key and passkey and every recovery code, ends every session of the user, and records `warden.identity.mfa.reset` with counts (`totp_removed`, `webauthn_removed`, `recovery_codes_removed`, `sessions_ended`). The user's next password sign-in answers `mfa_enrolment_required` where the session policy requires a second factor, and they enrol again. A user with nothing enrolled is a 204 too, still audited. `DELETE /users/{user_id}/totp` removes TOTP only and leaves keys.
